papers.title: Testing CCZ-equivalence to permutations via projections of Walsh zero spaces, with applications to APN functions
papers.abstract: Whether almost perfect nonlinear (APN) permutations exist in even dimension $n\ge 8$ is a long-standing open question, the big APN problem. The only example known in even dimension, on six bits, was found from a quadratic APN function that is not itself a permutation, by Carlet--Charpin--Zinoviev (CCZ) equivalence. It is therefore natural to test APN functions for CCZ-equivalence to a permutation. This amounts to finding two complementary $n$-dimensional subspaces among the zeros of the Walsh transform, which lie in $\mathbb{F}_2^{2n}$. A known necessary condition only uses their projections to $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and cannot decide every case. We give an exact test for functions whose Walsh supports are affine, including all quadratic functions. It reconstructs the subspaces from their projections, through searches for subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and for constrained bilinear maps. On the benchmarked functions in dimension twelve, it lists them $39$ to $55$ times faster than the generic search of the commonly used sboxU library. We then study the functions $x^3+a^{-1}\mathrm{Tr}(a^3x^9)$, which G\"olo\u{g}lu and Pavl\r{u} proved not to be CCZ-equivalent to permutations when $4$ divides $n$. With their result, our computations show that this holds for every even $n\le 24$. In dimension $18$ the necessary condition is satisfied, and the new test decides the case. We conjecture this for every even dimension. We also compile $25$ classes of quadratic APN functions in dimension ten from published instances, with equivalence certificates. No function in these classes or in their switching closure is CCZ-equivalent to a permutation. All code and data are public.

papers.title: Polynomial Sample Complexity of Noninteractive Simulation over Finite Alphabets
papers.abstract: We study noninteractive simulation from a finite correlated source. Alice and Bob observe independent copies of the source and generate outputs without communication. We give a quantitative construction for arbitrary finite output alphabets: for every fixed source, a joint law that is simulable with arbitrarily many samples can be approximated using a number of samples polynomial jointly in the output alphabet sizes and the inverse accuracy. We first study binary outputs. A one-sided Wright--Fisher comparison gives a source-dependent explicit exponent and a finite-head Gaussian-threshold representation. We then handle arbitrary finite output alphabets through averaged influence regularity, simplex-preserving Gaussian moment lifting, and a common Gaussian projection for all correlated-prefix states. The sample exponent is independent of the output alphabet sizes. For a concrete biased binary source we certify an explicit exponent below $19$.

papers.title: An Explicit Below Half Threshold Bound for the Local Leakage Resilience of Shamir's Secret Sharing Scheme
papers.abstract: As a fundamental cryptographic primitive, secret sharing distributes a secret among multiple parties and allows certain authorized parties to recover the secret while preventing unauthorized parties from knowing the secret. However, local leakage from each party member allows an adversary to learn partial information from each share, which is not guaranteed by traditional security. In this paper, we study bounds on the reconstruction threshold of Shamir's secret sharing scheme over prime fields against arbitrary 1-bit local leakage. We show that, for all sufficiently large $n$ and every prime $p>n$, the $(n,t)$-Shamir's scheme is $\exp(-\Omega(n))$-resilient whenever $t/n\geq 0.489$, for any choice of distinct nonzero evaluation points. Our proof refines the dual-code list recovery analysis and combines complementary Fourier estimates according to the support sizes and biases of the leakage functions, yielding an improved explicit reconstruction threshold bound.

papers.title: On Relative Greedy Weights
papers.abstract: Relative greedy weights were introduced by Li and Liu in [19] as a measure of information leakage in coordinated two-party wire-tap channels of type II when the adversary follows a greedy strategy. Their definition can be viewed as a relative version of the CEZ greedy weights, which are only locally greedy. In this paper, we revisit the concept of greediness and relative greediness introducing new measures, and we discuss other perhaps more relevant applications of relative greedy weights than the coordinated two-party wire-tap channel of type II. We pay special attention to bottom-up greedy weights, which correspond to an adversary with an ultimate greedy approach, and we present families of nested codes for which such weights are larger than the relative CEZ greedy weights.

papers.title: New Classes of CCZ-Inequivalent APN Functions with Boomerang Uniformity One in Odd Characteristic: Differential and Boomerang Spectra
papers.abstract: Let $q=p^n>3$ be an odd prime power and let $g:\F_q\to\F_q$ be an even perfect nonlinear (PN) function with $g(0)=0$. We construct almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions $G_{\lambda,M}(x)=g(x)+M(x)+\lambda(x^{q-1}-1)$, where $\lambda\in\F_q^*$, $-\lambda\notin g(\F_q)$, and $M$ is an $\F_p$-linearized permutation polynomial. These one-point modifications of $g+M$ have boomerang uniformity one, the smallest possible value for APN functions in odd characteristic. We give complete differential and boomerang spectrum formulas and obtain closed-form evaluations for selected constructions based on Coulter--Matthews monomials and Dembowski--Ostrom polynomials. For $q>7$, comparison of differential spectra establishes CCZ-inequivalence to all APN monomial families listed in the paper and every APN binomial in the original Ness--Helleseth family or its extension by Zeng et al. We characterize CCZ-equivalence within our construction, showing that any two linearly inequivalent even PN functions over the same field yield CCZ-inequivalent APN functions. We obtain three pairwise CCZ-inequivalent APN functions with boomerang uniformity one over $\F_{p^{15\ell}}$ for every $\ell\ge1$, six over $\F_{p^{120r}}$ for every $r\ge1$, and unbounded numbers of such classes in characteristic three. We further prove that CCZ-equivalence and EA-equivalence coincide for functions at Hamming distance at most $m$ from a PN function, provided that $m(m+1)<q-q/p$. We also show that all our APN functions have the maximal possible algebraic degree $n(p-1)$. Finally, we exhibit both CCZ-equivalent and CCZ-inequivalent APN pairs with boomerang uniformity one at Hamming distance one.

papers.title: Laws of Learning Dynamics and the Core of Learners
papers.abstract: We formulate an algorithm-independent theory of learning dynamics for individual models and ensembles. We establish a conservation law, the vanishing of predictive entropy under successful learning, quantitative entropy and core-expansion bounds, and calibration and finite-sample validation results for identifying reliable predictions. These results motivate a two-generation ensemble that uses Jensen-Shannon (JS) disagreement to route uncertain inputs to specialized learners. CIFAR-10 experiments examine controlled perturbations, distribution shifts, and adversarial attacks. On a heterogeneous test environment, routing improves accuracy over probability averaging while keeping core accuracy near 95%. For adversarial defense, we consider a query-only black-box setting: the attacker can query the overall prediction function but does not know a particular internal decomposition into learners and routing rules. Our current attacks use a fixed-initial-route gradient, which is accurate for a single-step attack when the route remains unchanged, but may deviate from actual multi-step attacks, especially for large perturbations. We evaluate our two-layer defense against this approximation; whether additional adversarially trained layers improve resistance to stronger multi-step attacks remains for future study.

papers.title: A Communication-Theoretic Framework for LLM Agents: Cost-Aware Adaptive Reliability
papers.abstract: Agents built on large language models (LLMs) rely on reliability techniques such as retry, majority voting, and self-consistency developed in parallel rather than within a common analytical framework. We observe that an LLM sampled at temperature $T$ is a discrete stochastic channel $p(y \mid x)$ in the sense of Shannon's coding theory, and use this identity as the entry point for such a framework. Each of these techniques is a special case of one of six classical reliability operators: diversity combining, hybrid retransmission, iterative generator-critic decoding, rateless sampling, structured redundant verification, and difficulty-adaptive routing. Within the framework we give two closed-form results, a noise-variance threshold above which uniform averaging beats quality-weighted averaging and a contractivity criterion for generator-critic refinement, and turn each into a design rule checkable before committing compute. We further introduce a cost-aware semantic-nearest-neighbor router whose single Lagrangian knob traverses the quality-cost frontier without retraining. Across six local and cloud channel configurations, no fixed model-technique-budget choice dominates. On a 300-item hard split of MMLU, GSM8K, and HumanEval, the router occupies the empirical Pareto frontier: at matched quality its normalized cost is $\approx$56% lower than the best fixed technique, and at matched cost it improves quality by $\approx$7% (26% over single-shot decoding). Judge-free grading of 6,900 outputs confirms that the judge tracks correctness at the item level and that the router's advantage over a fixed policy persists at most cost settings; with internal reasoning enabled, the gain of external refinement shrinks but remains significant for our incremental-redundancy operator. These results argue for consolidating reliability techniques into a single tunable layer informed by channel coding.

papers.title: Fast Rates for Offline Contextual Bandits with Forward-KL Regularization under Single-Policy Concentrability
papers.abstract: \emph{Kullback-Leibler} (KL) regularization is ubiquitous in reinforcement learning algorithms in the form of \emph{reverse} or \emph{forward} KL. Recent studies have demonstrated $\epsilon^{-1}$-type fast rates for decision making under reverse KL regularization, in contrast to the standard $\epsilon^{-2}$-type sample complexity. However, for forward-KL-regularized objectives, existing statistical analyses are either not applicable or result in $\tilde{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ slow rates. We take the first step towards addressing this problem via a streamlined analysis of forward-KL-regularized offline CBs. We give the first $\tilde{O}(\epsilon^{-1})$ upper bounds in tabular and general function approximation settings, both under notions of \emph{single-policy concentrability}. In particular, our convex-analytical pipeline unifies these settings by exploiting the pessimism principle in a novel way and completely bypasses the proof routines in previous works based on the mean value theorem, which might be of independent interest. Moreover, we provide rate-optimal lower bounds, manifesting the tightness of our upper bounds in terms of statistical rates. Our lower bounds also demonstrate that the forward-KL-regularized sample complexity recovers the unregularized slow rate in the low-regularization regime, similarly to the reverse-KL regularization.

papers.title: Linear Set Reconciliation with $O(d)$ Additive Redundancy
papers.abstract: In set reconciliation, two parties holding sets $A, B \subseteq [n]$ with $|A \triangle B| \le d$ seek to recover their symmetric difference from short $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear sketches, which is equivalent to recovering a $d$-sparse vector $x = \mathbf{1}_{A \triangle B} \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ from its syndrome $Hx \in \mathbb{F}_2^m$. While the information-theoretic counting bound requires $L(n,d) := \log \sum_{i=0}^d \binom{n}{i} = d\log(n/d) + \Theta(d)$ bits, existing polynomial-time schemes either use at least $d\lceil\log(n+1)\rceil$ bits (algebraic sketches, leaving an $\Omega(d\log d)$-bit gap) or incur a multiplicative $(1+\delta)L(n,d)$ overhead (peeling-based sketches), raising the question of whether $L(n,d) + O(d)$ bits is achievable with fast updates and decoding. We construct a public-coin randomized $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear sketch of length $L(n,d) + O(d) + \lambda\log^{O(1)} n$ that recovers each fixed input of weight at most $d$ with probability at least $1 - 2^{-\lambda}$, with $\log^{O(1)} n$ update time and $d\exp(O((\log\log n)^2)) = dn^{o(1)}$ worst-case decoding time. In particular, for $n \le 2^{\operatorname{polylog}(d)}$ and $\lambda \le d^{1-\Omega(1)}$, this achieves $L(n,d) + O(d)$ bits with $\operatorname{polylog}(d)$ update time and $d^{1+o(1)}$ decoding time. Our construction encodes $d$ permuted rows via randomly scaled Pinsketch syndromes and sketches the resulting bit array column by column. Decoding columns sequentially from prefix predictions cancels recovered rows and exposes undecided rows as decoder-side hints, reducing each column to a hinted sparse recovery problem that we solve via a recursive sketch, HintSketch.

papers.title: Fresh Enough to Decide: Age of Intelligence for Cost-Aware Model Synchronization in Dynamic IoT Systems
papers.abstract: Resource-constrained IoT devices cache learned models for real-time decisions, but frequent updates incur substantial bandwidth, energy, and service overhead. Because decision-relevant model differences need not grow with elapsed time, we define Age of Intelligence (AoInt) as a model-version-relative, client-specific, and action utility distortion, and formulate synchronization as a tradeoff between stale-decision regret and refresh cost. Furthermore, we develop Kullback-Leibler-aware AoInt Synchronization (KL-AoIntSync), which accumulates output-distribution changes using client-specific unlabeled probes, whereas Parameter-aware AoInt Synchronization (Param-AoIntSync) uses a server-broadcast scalar parameter change. Then, we establish pathwise guarantees with fixed client distributions, action sets, and utilities. The numerical results show that calibrated Param-AoIntSync reduces joint synchronization cost by 6.15% relative to an Instant-Parameters policy while performing comparably to KL-AoIntSync.

papers.title: Topology and Information in Regularized Transport on Graphs
papers.abstract: We study how two geometries of mass on a finite graph interact: the information geometry of the generalized entropy $F_q$ used for regularized transport, and the arithmetic of divisors governed by the Riemann--Roch theorem of Baker and Norine and by the Jacobian. Because the correction term of $F_q$ is affine, $F_q$-regularization at strength $\gamma$ is Tsallis regularization at temperature $\gamma/q$. Over the reals, chip-firing connects all configurations of equal degree, so the Jacobian enters transport only through integrality. We introduce the transport defect, the worst-case cost of steering $d$ chips towards a target by chip-firing, and prove $1/d\le\delta_{\TV}(D)\le(d-r(D))/d=(g-1-r(K-D))/d\le\min(1,g/d)$ whenever $g\ge1$; vertex multiplicities give a lower bound and an equality criterion. A regularized topological gap $\Gamma_{q,\gamma}(D,E)$ tends to the chip-move defect as $\gamma\to0$, lies in an explicit window, has a high-temperature slope given by Tsallis coupling entropies, and admits a positive regime if and only if $g\ge1$. Dual potentials certify exactly the convex relaxation of a linear system; the remainder is an integrality gap. Zeros in optimal plans occur only for $q>1$, by a mechanism different from the sign change of $\Gamma$. Exact computations on $1784$ divisor classes find the rank bound $(d-r(D))/d$ attained in $1769$ of them, an observed frequency. Experiments on honeycomb and Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi networks with $10^2$ to $10^5$ nodes test the statements on regularized plans, not $\Gamma$; over $10^3\le n\le10^5$ their transport costs are consistent with growth like $n^{1/2}$ and $\log n$, respectively.

papers.title: QoS-Aware Energy-Efficient Sub-THz Near-Field Multiuser Hybrid MIMO Systems Employing Circular Arrays
papers.abstract: Near-field communications have emerged as a promising technology for future sixth-generation (6G) networks. However, designing energy-efficient hybrid beamfocusing schemes for multiuser (MU) systems remains challenging due to the non-convex quality-of-service (QoS) constraints and hardware limitations of hybrid architectures. In this paper, we investigate a hybrid massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) architecture for a near-field sub-THz MU downlink system employing a large uniform circular array (UCA) at the base station. A QoS-aware transmit power minimization problem is formulated for energy-efficient beamfocusing and addressed through a two-stage penalty-driven joint optimization (PDJO) framework, where auxiliary variables are introduced to reformulate the QoS constraints into second-order cone (SOC) constraints. Furthermore, a near-field polar-domain codebook is developed via joint angle- and distance-domain sampling. We establish that the fully digital (FD) beamfocuser lies within the column space of the proposed codebook, enabling hybrid precoder design to be formulated as a multiple measurement vector (MMV)-based sparse approximation problem. The formulated problem is then solved using a low-complexity simultaneous orthogonal matching pursuit (SOMP) algorithm under hardware and transmit power constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves spectral- and energy-efficiency performance close to the ideal FD beamfocusing scheme while providing a favorable trade-off between hardware complexity and system performance.

papers.title: DNA-MGC+: A versatile codec for reliable and resource-efficient data storage on synthetic DNA
papers.abstract: The biochemical processes underlying DNA data storage, including synthesis, amplification, and sequencing, are inherently noisy, leading to insertion, deletion, and substitution errors as well as sequence dropouts that challenge reliable data retrieval. Here we introduce DNA-MGC+, a DNA storage codec designed for reliable and resource-efficient retrieval under diverse operating conditions. We evaluate DNA-MGC+ across various in silico and in vitro settings. In comparison with selected representative codecs, the results show that DNA-MGC+ consistently improves key performance metrics under explicit reliability constraints, including required sequencing depth, read cost, decoding time, storage density, and error-correction capability. In silico experiments show that DNA-MGC+ supports reliable decoding at error rates up to 24% for a 15-KB file, while separate scalability experiments demonstrate reliable decoding of files up to 200 MB at a 5% error rate. In vitro experiments involving a 24-KB file and electrochemical synthesis show that different DNA-MGC+ configurations achieve minimum sequencing depths below 3x and read costs below 3.5 nts/bit under both Illumina and Nanopore sequencing.

papers.title: Cross-Domain Channel Estimation for MU-MIMO-OFDM
papers.abstract: Conventional channel estimation for multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) relies on the pilot interpolation without explicitly identifying the sparse delay-angle (DA) components. To exploit DA sparsity while maintaining backward compatibility with existing MIMO-OFDM systems, we propose a cross-domain channel estimation scheme for multiuser MIMO-OFDM (MU-MIMO-OFDM) systems. The scheme exploits the circular convolution structure in the DA domain to identify candidate DA pairs by correlating delay-domain observations with DA pilot responses. These pairs and the known pilots then define a time-frequency (TF) dictionary for refining the DA coefficients from TF observations through least-squares or sparsity-regularized fitting. The refined coefficients and candidate pairs reconstruct the aggregate channel across antennas and subcarriers aligning with the geometric channel model. Numerical results show approximately 10 dB and 7 dB lower normalized mean-square error than the conventional OFDM estimation schemes for integer and fractional delay and angle indices, respectively.

papers.title: Learning-Assisted Beamforming Optimization for Hybrid XL-RIS-Aided Communication
papers.abstract: Hybrid active-passive extremely large-scale reconfigurable intelligent surface (XL-RIS) architectures mitigate the double-hop path loss of passive RIS while enabling near-field spatial energy focusing, but impose a computationally intensive mixed discrete-continuous beamforming design problem under strict radio-frequency (RF) power constraints. This paper investigates a hybrid XL-RIS-assisted downlink multi-user multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) system in the near-field regime. The joint optimization of the base station (BS) precoder, discrete XL-RIS phase shifts, and active-element amplification gains is addressed via a discrete coordinate ascent (DCA)-based alternating optimization (AO) framework, in which discrete variables are updated through local index-domain searches and the BS precoder is derived in closed form via a noise-aware minimum mean-square error (MMSE) criterion. To reduce the per-sample computational cost for XL-RIS apertures, a deep unfolding (DU) framework is proposed as a low-complexity alternative, unrolling a fixed number of Riemannian gradient ascent steps on the sum-rate objective and recovering the discrete phase configuration via quantized phasor projection, with one learnable step size per layer trained in a self-supervised manner. Numerical results under near-field spherical-wave channel models confirm that the DU framework achieves sum-rate performance close to the AO scheme with substantially lower and nearly constant runtime, and that both schemes consistently outperform manifold optimization under discrete hardware constraints.

papers.title: Performance Analysis of Entanglement Swapping DV-QKD over MIMO FSO Channels
papers.abstract: This paper studies multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) free-space optical (FSO) quantum communication systems employing polarization-encoded discrete-variable quantum key distribution (DV-QKD), based on entanglement swapping, with the goal of extending secure communications beyond the reach of a direct link. The FSO channels are subject to atmospheric absorption, diffraction, beam wander, pointing errors, and turbulence-induced fading, while background noise and detector imperfections degrade the performance. An eavesdropper controlling the channels and the relay is also considered. To analyze the performance of the considered system, both hops MIMO channels are decomposed into parallel spatial eigenchannels via singular value decomposition (SVD), photon loss is modeled using Kraus operators, and a threshold-detector model is developed for the relay. Based on these models, closed-form per-eigenchannel expressions for the relay gain are derived, which are then used to obtain expressions for the quantum bit error rate (QBER) and the secret key rate (SKR). Numerical results demonstrate that entanglement swapping maintains a low QBER over longer distances than direct transmission, extending the communication range beyond the noise-limited cutoff of the direct link, at the cost of a lower SKR at short distances. The crossover distance beyond which entanglement swapping prevails is determined mainly by the background noise and the detector technology, and it is demonstrated to increase with MIMO configurations. Moreover, the reach gain is shown to be maximized for a midpoint relay. Finally, since each swapping event requires a single-pair emission from both sources, a near-deterministic entangled-photon source is required, which spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources do not provide at practical key rates, whereas MIMO substantially relaxes this requirement.

papers.title: BP-based qLDPC Decoding under Long-range Correlated Noise: Trapping Configurations and Prior Mismatch
papers.abstract: We study the robustness of two state-of-the-art BP-based qLDPC decoders, Relay-BP and beam search, designed for independent noise when applied to spatially correlated noise with unchanged single-mechanism error probabilities. We generate correlated errors with a hidden Gaussian Markov random field, which lets us control the strength and range of the correlation while keeping every marginal error probability exact. This setting complements correlation-aware decoding: it asks how existing decoders perform when their assumed joint error model is mismatched. Across multiple tested circuits and code instances that we simulated, we observe that correlations can change logical error rates by orders of magnitude, reduce the finite-size distance advantage, and alter the relative ranking of Relay-BP, beam search, and BP-OSD. On one of the two tested circuits, Relay-BP and beam search become worse than BP-OSD, and increasing relay memory or beam width does not compensate for the degradation. Configuration analysis indicates that correlation primarily increases the probability of trapping configurations that are known to challenge these decoders; at matched error weight, correlated errors still cause decoding failures several times more often than i.i.d. errors. Finally, supplying the decoders with the marginals conditioned on the hidden field recovers most of the lost performance in the tested settings identifying prior mismatch as a major contributor to performance degradation under correlation.

papers.title: Quantum channel bounds for constant-composition codes
papers.abstract: We extend the quantum-channel optimization of Alrabiah and Guruswami to $q$-ary constant-composition codes. We study explicit channel and flag constructions that recover selected classical asymptotic upper bounds, including the Ben-Haim--Litsyn, moving-subspace and Horn-channel bounds. We give two equivalent formulations, Gram and flag, and prove stability of the obtained upper bounds under permutation transport and generalized shortening. A hierarchy defined by bounding the output-state ranks within each flag improves strictly between consecutive levels at every composition and every positive distance below the Plotkin threshold. We provide finite matrix parametrizations of these bounds (i.e., the number of variables does not depend on the length of codes under consideration). Numerical optimization rapidly produces improvements over the known asymptotic upper bounds throughout all tested nonbinary parameter ranges. For rational input data, each finite level admits near-optimal feasible rational descriptions of polynomial length. Their feasibility can be checked exactly and their objective values computed to any prescribed accuracy in polynomial time; the associated threshold problem with a prescribed gap belongs to $\mathsf{PromiseNP}$.

papers.title: Efficient SC-Flip Decoding for Polar Codes through Decision-Boundary Normalization
papers.abstract: Accurate first erroneous position (FEP) identification is key to improving the error-correction performance of successive cancellation flip (SCF) decoding. However, FEP identification remains challenging with a limited number of re-decoding attempts. To address this issue, we propose decision-boundary normalization (DBN) to improve FEP identification and develop a novel DBN-SCF decoding algorithm. DBN normalizes the magnitude of each decision log-likelihood ratio (LLR) by the standard deviation predicted by the Gaussian approximation (GA) for the corresponding bit-channel. This allows a single normalized threshold to be shared across bit-channels within each code configuration, giving it a consistent statistical meaning and avoiding per-channel calibration. DBN-SCF decoding selects candidate flip positions from the information set in the natural successive cancellation (SC) decoding order using a threshold, without sorting. Moreover, DBN-SCF decoding achieves better error-correction performance with a limited number of re-decoding attempts. It also requires lower average decoding complexity than existing SCF decoding methods at a comparable level of error-correction performance.

papers.title: Quantum synchronizable codes, polynomial and quasi-polynomial shifts
authors: Miguel de los R\'ios de Antonio
papers.abstract: Quantum synchronizable codes protect quantum information against Pauli errors and against misalignments of the block boundaries. Almost all known constructions use cyclic codes, because the channel shifts the transmitted block cyclically. We study what happens when the algebraic shift of the code differs from the physical one. When one uses a twisted padding, constacyclic codes synchronize at no cost, and they are the only polycyclic codes with this property for a linear padding. For the other polycyclic codes, we measure the cost of each misaligned position, and we show that the phase damage it causes can be corrected as erasures. Using annihilator duality, we extend the construction to quasi-polycyclic codes, in which the cost is confined to a single block. We prove that the usual quasi-cyclic families have a distance bound that does not grow with the length, and show that quasi-polycyclic codes over repeated-root trinomials overcome it, giving synchronizable codes with larger dimension and distance than the known synchronizable codes of the same length.

papers.title: Optimal Sampling and Transmission Policy for Information Freshness in Gossip Networks
papers.abstract: We study the optimal sampling and transmission policies for a transmitter communicating with n gossiping receivers with the objective of tracking a source's status over time using a semantic freshness metric: Version Age of Information (VAoI). The transmitter observes the version changes in the source, and can acquire a new information version by paying a sampling cost. The receivers gossip, allowing information exchange among each other without direct transmission. Gossiping can save on transmission cost, but it may propagate stale version information, necessitating transmitter intervention. With imperfect communication links, we formulate an infinite horizon average cost Markov Decision Process (MDP) in order to jointly optimize receivers' VAoIs, sampling and transmission costs in a time slotted fully connected (FC) gossip network. We first solve the MDP using Relative Value Iteration (RVI) algorithm. Then, we prove that the sampling decision has a threshold structure in the transmitter VAoI. Further, under reliable gossiping links, we show that transmission and idling has an VAoI-difference threshold structure with minimum VAoI activation. Numerical results obtained using RVI show that the optimal policy consistently outperforms natural baselines. These results characterize how source sampling, direct transmission, and receiver gossip should be jointly coordinated for cost-aware semantic freshness in gossip networks.

papers.title: Iterative Interference Cancellation for Near-Field XL-MIMO Networks with LoS Channels
papers.abstract: In extra-large multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems, near-field users experience spherical wavefront propagation, offering higher spatial resolution than far-field plane-wave models, but complicating signal detection and interference cancellation. Under line-of-sight conditions, we propose a weighted-rate successive interference cancellation (WR-SIC) scheme whose ordering metric exploits the enhanced spatial degrees of freedom of near-field propagation to prioritize users with stronger channels. An iterative detection and decoding (IDD) scheme with LDPC coding is then developed. Simulations in hybrid near- and far-field deployments show that the proposed WR-SIC and IDD schemes improve bit-error and sum rates over existing schemes

papers.title: A Characterization of $q$-Ary $2$-Designs and a $3$-Design Obstruction for Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}_k$ be the doubly extended Reed--Solomon code with parameters $[q+1,k,q-k+2]_q$, where $q\ge3$ is a prime power and $2\le k\le q$. We prove a conjecture of Wu and Zhou by showing that the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}_k$ do not form a $q$-ary $3$-design when $2\le k\le q-1$. Using shortening, we extend this obstruction to every nonempty weight class with $3\le w<q+1$. We also establish that each individual nonempty positive-weight class of $\mathcal{C}_k$ forms a $q$-ary $2$-design if and only if $\gcd(k-1,q-1)=1$. Consequently, every nonempty positive-weight class below full support has exact $q$-ary design strength $2$ when this coprimality condition holds, and $1$ otherwise.The three-design obstruction follows by applying a classical subset-product character identity to a marginal covering count for three prescribed nonzero symbols. The comparison between weights rests on a covering-count formulation of the classical MDS coset-weight relations. For every linear $[n,k,d]_q$ MDS code with $2\le k\le n-1$, this formulation shows that the $q$-ary $2$-design property at any one nonempty positive weight is equivalent to the same property at every nonempty positive weight.More generally, for $2\le t\le\min\{k,d\}$, we prove that the $q$-ary $t$-design property at any $t-1$ distinct nonempty positive weights forces it at all nonempty positive weights.

papers.title: Beating the Probabilistic Bound for Hashing and Improving Lower Bounds for Trifferent Codes
papers.abstract: We improve the probabilistic lower bounds on the rates of hash codes and list-recoverable codes. For perfect $q$-hashing, we prove $R_q>B_q$ for every $q\geq 3$. Our main result concerns non-perfect hashing. For every $q\geq 4$, we prove $R_{q,3}>B_{q,3}+\frac{1}{250000}.$ In particular, the case $q=9$, combined with the Tetra code, strictly improves the K\"orner-Marton lower bound $R_3\geq \frac14\log(9/5)$ for trifferent codes. We also extend the method to $(p,2,3)$-list recovery. For every $q\geq 4$ and $0\leq p<\frac{q-2}{12(q-1)}$, we prove $R_q^{\mathrm{LR}}(p)>B_q^{\mathrm{LR}}(p)$. For every fixed $0\leq p<1/18$, the rate improvement is bounded below by a positive constant independent of $q\geq 4$. The same holds for every fixed $0\le p<1/12$ when $q$ is sufficiently large.

papers.title: Joint Design of Communication and Control in Center-Fed Pinching-Antenna Systems
papers.abstract: An analytical and optimization framework for the joint design of communication and control (JDCC) in a center-fed pinching-antenna system (C-PASS) is proposed. Within this framework, the mathematical coupling between data throughput and closed-loop control cost is characterized for JDCC. The analysis captures the mutual interference between concurrently transmitted data and control streams during uplink state uploading and downlink command delivery. Based on this coupling, an achievable communication-control performance region is established for C-PASS. Accordingly, a throughput maximization problem is formulated to jointly optimize digital and pinching beamforming subject to control-cost constraints. To address this problem, an alternating optimization algorithm is developed based on constraint reformulation and resource decomposition. The proposed framework reveals how control requirements shape achievable data throughput, guiding the joint beamforming design. Numerical results demonstrate that 1) the proposed C-PASS design achieves 110.2\% higher frame-average throughput than conventional PASS, and 2) the proposed concurrent data-control transmission protocol increases frame-average throughput by up to 66.7\% over separated transmission.

papers.title: CHANNELS4WORLD: An Environment-Scale Dataset for Wireless Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Wireless foundation models learn reusable representations across tasks, configurations, and deployment environments. Their pretraining requires environmental breadth, yet wireless datasets often sample few sites densely. We introduce Channels4World, a scene-centered dataset of 100,000 distinct outdoor RF scenes and a procedural method for generating them. Each scene links a generated environment and RF material assignments to 32 base-station (BS) positions, 16,384 UE positions, and aligned variable-length multipath and ordered interaction records at 3.5 and 7~GHz. The corpus comprises 52.43 billion physical BS-UE pairs, 104.86 billion frequency-specific evaluations, and a 29.14-TB packaged payload. Scene identity aligns geometry, placements, channels, and interactions across frequencies, allowing environmental breadth and within-scene observation density to vary independently. The public release offers predefined subsets at multiple scales and separate access to corpus components. A deterministic 90K/10K scene-level train-test split keeps both frequencies and all scene components together. We characterize morphology, RF materials, and transceiver placement across three generation profiles. Controlled propagation and path-retention analyses show that diffraction materially affects retained-link availability and multipath structure, while the retention policy reduces storage substantially with little loss in represented aggregate power. Under matched training exposure, models trained on broader scene collections perform better on held-out scenes, although an equal-episode control shows that scene count alone cannot explain the gain. By making environmental breadth explicit and controllable, Channels4World supports the development and evaluation of wireless foundation models for generalization across deployment environments.

papers.title: Sharp Rates for Optimal Recovery of Bandlimited Functions from Localized Oversampling
papers.abstract: It is well-known that one can recover a function $f$ bandlimited to $[-\delta,\delta]$ ( $0<\delta<\pi$) from its finite sample data $f(j),-n\le j\le n$, with an approximation error exponentially decaying to zero as $n$ tends to infinity. Various regularized Shannon sampling formula have been proposed to achieve such exponential approximation. So far the best rate has been $$ O\biggl(\frac1{\sqrt{n}}\exp(-(\pi-\delta)n)\biggr). $$ We establish that the optimal recovery algorithm in the worst-case scenario achieves an approximation error $\rho_{n,\delta}$ satisfying $$ c_* \frac1{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\frac\delta 4)^{2n+1/2}\le \rho_{n,\delta}\le C^* \frac1{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\frac\delta 4)^{2n+1/2}, \quad 0<\delta\leq\pi,\quad n\geq1, $$ where $c_*,C^*$ are positive constants independent of $n$ and $\delta$. This result identifies the best possible exponential rate to reconstruct bandlimited functions from two-sided finite oversampling data. In other words, $$ \rho_{n,\delta} \asymp \frac{\tan\frac\delta 4}{\sqrt{n}}\exp\bigl(-c_\delta(\pi-\delta)n\bigr), $$ where $c_\delta$ is strictly decreasing on $(0,\pi]$ and $$ \lim_{\delta\to\pi^-}c_\delta=1,\ \lim_{\delta\to 0^+}c_\delta=+\infty. $$ We also make the new finding that one can also reconstruct $f$ bandlimited to $[-\delta,\delta]$ with exponentially decaying error from one-sided sample data $f(j)$, $1\le j\le n$, and the sharp rate of approximation error $\rho_{n,\delta}'$ of the optimal algorithm is $$ \rho_{n,\delta}' \asymp \sqrt{\delta/\pi}\sin^n(\delta/2). $$

papers.title: Compression of Sources with Memory and Private Random Access
papers.abstract: Private local decoding imposes a stringent constraint on compression: the codeword bits used to recover a source symbol must reveal nothing about the remaining symbols beyond what the recovered symbol itself reveals. For memoryless sources, this constraint is known to be compatible with entropy-rate compression. We show that the same holds for any stationary ergodic source over a finite alphabet. Specifically, every rate above the entropy rate is achievable with exact privacy and error-free local decoding on a set of source sequences whose probability tends to one. In contrast, we exhibit non-ergodic sources for which private local decoding incurs a strictly positive rate penalty.

papers.title: Binary Belief Propagation Fixed Points: Finiteness, Rigidity, and Topological Complexity
papers.abstract: A fixed finite binary Ising model has only finitely many admissible complex belief propagation fixed points, even at degenerate parameter values. Families of positive fixed points obtained by varying external fields can nevertheless have nontrivial topology. We study this distinction through the external-field projection. For a fixed field, we prove finiteness by bounding the pole orders of the magnetizations on a hypothetical complex solution curve. The generic degree on the support graph then bounds the total local multiplicity. A graph has a single smooth real line as its full positive response for every choice of positive couplings, base field, and strictly positive sweep direction exactly when it contains no two vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs of cycle rank at least two. Two such subgraphs suffice to create a circular component. For a plane obtained by varying two vertex fields, connected simple bipartite cubic graphs with one uniform coupling and a universal bound on the fixed fields realize every genus. The minimum number of vertices grows logarithmically in the genus, by a matching algebraic upper bound on Betti numbers. Finally, we certify the complete field discriminant of an eighteen-vertex product model and recover its torus component's genus from the counts of distinct roots on all field cells. The three main theorems, including the logarithmic size bounds, are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

papers.title: Bounds and Constructions for Optimal Wide-Gap Frequency Hopping Sequences
papers.abstract: In a frequency-hopping (FH) system, to reduce interference to the received signal, each user's frequency hopping sequence (FHS) shall have wide-gap property. In this paper, we update the upper bounds on the minimum gaps of optimal uniform wide-gap frequency hopping sequences (WGFHS) with parameters $(v,s,\lambda;e)$ where $v=ks, k\ge 3, \lambda=k$ and $s\ge k(k-1)+1$ is odd. We completely prove the existence of such WGFHSs for $k\le 3$.
